Let $y^(^) = β^(^)_{0} + β^(^)_{1}x = 3.5 + 5x$ be the regression line fitted using a sample $(x_{1}, y_{1}), …, (x_{20}, y_{20})$ of $n = 20$ paired observations. Assuming that all conditions for the simple regression model are satisfied, the mean square error of the model is $8$, and $S_{xx} = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)(x_{i} - x^(―))^{2} = 24$, find a $95%$ confidence interval for the slope of the regression line.

*Hint: Use the fact that $P(T > 2.101) = 0.025$, where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $18$ degrees of freedom. Also, the standard error for $β^(^)_{1}$ is given by $SE[β^(^)_{1}] = \sqrt{\frac{MSE}{S_{xx}}}$.*

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

Assuming that all conditions for the simple regression model are satisfied, the mean square error of the model is $0.95$, and $S_{xx} = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)(x_{i} - x^(―))^{2} = 143$, find a $95%$ confidence interval for the slope of the regression line.
